landing.heroLead: Motor insurance for Azerbaijan. Change any detail below and the PolisGo pricing engine reprices it instantly — with every factor on the table.

pricing.lead: One base rate, six multipliers, a cap on the extremes. The same arithmetic runs when a policy is issued — only then on verified data.

base.title: Base rate
base.body: Each product starts from its own rate: the cost of covering an average driver for a year.

risk.title: Five risk factors
risk.body: Engine capacity, driver age, years of experience, vehicle age and claims history each add a multiplier above or below ×1.00.

cap.title: A cap on risk
cap.body: The five risk multipliers are combined and held between ×0.50 and ×3.00, so no profile is priced out or given away.

term.title: Term
term.body: The price is pro-rated by month. Terms under twelve months carry a 10% loading for administration.

rounding.title: One rounding
rounding.body: Everything stays at full precision until the end, then the premium is rounded once, to the qiyəpik.

coverage.lead: Products and base rates come straight from the PolisGo API.
coverage.caption: Coverage by product

rows.ownDamage: Damage to your own car in an accident

claims.lead: Four steps, each recorded in the claim’s history so you always know where it stands.

submit.title: Submit
submit.body: Report the incident online: the date, what happened, the amount, and photos or documents.

review.title: Review
review.body: An adjuster takes the claim, checks the documents and the policy, and keeps you informed.

decision.title: Decision
decision.body: An approved amount up to what you claimed, or a written reason if the claim is rejected.

payout.title: Payout
payout.body: Approved claims are paid out and marked paid. The full history stays on record.

final.q: Is the price on this page final?
final.a: No — it is an indicative estimate. When a policy is issued, the premium is recalculated from your verified customer and vehicle records.

differ.q: Why could my final premium differ?
differ.a: At issue the engine uses the data stored on your account, including approved or paid claims from the last three years, instead of what was typed into the calculator.

cap.a: The five risk factors are multiplied together and the result is kept between ×0.50 and ×3.00. It protects both very low-risk and very high-risk drivers from extreme prices.

term.q: Can I insure a car for less than a year?
term.a: Yes, for 1 to 12 months. The price is pro-rated by month, plus a 10% loading for terms shorter than a year.

claim.q: How do I make a claim?
claim.a: Sign in, choose the policy, describe the incident and upload photos or documents. An adjuster reviews it, and every status change is recorded.

licensed.a: No. PolisGo is a portfolio project that demonstrates an insurance platform; quotes illustrate its pricing engine.

help.title: Help and questions
help.lead: Short answers about buying, managing and renewing your policies.

price.a: A base rate for the type of cover is multiplied by factors for the engine, your age and driving experience, the vehicle’s age and your claims in the last three years, then adjusted for the term. Every policy page shows the factors it was priced with.

exact.q: Is the price in the purchase steps final?
exact.a: Yes. It is calculated from the details on your account and the chosen vehicle, the same way as when the policy is issued. The calculator on the main site is only an estimate for any driver.

dates.a: Today or on any day in the next 60 days. Cover runs from the start date to the end date inclusive, for 1 to 12 months.

payment.a: No. PolisGo is a portfolio project and payments go through a demonstration gateway: no card is asked for and no money moves.

renew.q: How do I renew a policy?
renew.a: From 30 days before a policy ends, a reminder appears on your overview and under the bell. Renew opens the purchase with the same vehicle and cover, starting the day after the old policy ends.

certificate.a: Open the policy and choose Download certificate. It is created on your device as a PDF in the language you are using, and is available once the policy is paid.

expired.q: Why does a policy show as expired?
expired.a: Cover ends after its last day. From the next day the policy shows as Expired and stays in your list for your records.

cancel.q: What happens to an unpaid policy?
cancel.a: It stays unpaid until you pay it from its page. Once its start date has passed it can no longer be paid; buy a new one with a new date instead.

reminders.q: Will reminders reach my phone or email?
reminders.a: No. Reminders are shown only in the cabinet, under the bell and on the overview. Marking one as read hides the dot on every device you use.

details.q: Can I change my name or phone?
details.a: Yes, in Profile and settings. To correct your date of birth or licence date, contact support: they decide your premium.

password.q: How do I change my password?
password.a: In Profile and settings, enter your current password and a new one with 8–64 characters, an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter and a number.

preferences.q: Where are language and theme saved?
preferences.a: On this device. Change them in the header, in Profile and settings, or with Ctrl/⌘ + K.

claims.q: How do I file a claim?
claims.a: Open My claims and choose File a claim, or use the button on an active policy's page. Choose the policy, say when, where and what happened, estimate the damage, add photos if you have them, then check and file. Your answers are kept if the page reloads.

licensed.a: No. PolisGo is a portfolio project that demonstrates an insurance platform; its policies and certificates are not real insurance.

claimDocs.a: Clear photos of the damage and the scene, the other vehicle's plate, a police report or the accident form signed by both drivers, and a repair quote or invoice. JPG, PNG or PDF up to 5 MB each, 10 per claim. You can add more from the claim's page while it is open.

claimStatuses.q: What do the claim statuses mean?
claimStatuses.a: Submitted: waiting for an adjuster. Under review: an adjuster is assessing it. Approved: accepted, with the approved amount. Rejected: not covered; the adjuster's note says why. Paid out: the approved amount has been paid. Withdrawn: you took the claim back.

claimWithdraw.a: Yes, until an adjuster decides on it. Open the claim and choose Withdraw claim. It can't be undone; you can add a reason for the adjuster.

claimUpdates.q: How will I know the claim has moved?
claimUpdates.a: Every step appears in the claim's history and under the bell, with a dot until you read it. Nothing is sent by phone or email.

help.lead: How the staff desks work: the claims queue, decisions, your customers and exports.

queue.a: The shared queue of claims nobody has taken yet, and the claims you have taken. A claim another adjuster is reviewing is theirs, so it is not in your list.

takeReview.q: What happens when I start a review?
takeReview.a: The claim is assigned to you and leaves the shared queue. From then on only you, or an administrator, can approve or reject it.

decide.q: How do I approve or reject?
decide.a: Open the claim from “In my review”, choose the outcome and record it. An approval can be for the claimed amount or less, with at most two decimals.

reason.a: For a rejection, yes: the customer reads it on their claim page. For an approval a note is optional and also visible to the customer.

unavailable.a: The decision panel follows the claim’s status: review first, then approve or reject, then pay out. Each unavailable step says why, for example “Start the review first”.

conflict.q: What if someone changes the claim while I’m on it?
conflict.a: Your decision is refused rather than applied to facts you haven’t seen. The page loads the latest version and keeps your note, so you can check it and decide again.

pay.q: When is a claim paid out?
pay.a: After it is approved, from the claim page. The payout goes through the payment service for the approved amount; in this build it is a demonstration and no money moves.

book.a: The customers an administrator assigned to you. You see their details, the policies you sold them and the claims on those policies, and nobody else’s.

sell.q: How do I sell a policy to a customer?
sell.a: Open the customer and choose Sell a policy. The premium is calculated from their details, as when they buy online. Take the payment then, or leave the policy unpaid for them to pay.

agentClaims.q: Can I decide my customers’ claims?
agentClaims.a: No. Adjusters decide claims; you see their status on the customer’s page. You can file a claim for a customer on a policy you sold.

export.a: Every row that matches the current filters and sort, not just the page on screen, up to 5,000 rows.

exportExcel.q: Will Excel show Azerbaijani and Russian letters?
exportExcel.a: Yes: the file is UTF-8 with a byte-order mark. Values are comma-separated; if your Excel uses semicolons, open the file through Data → From Text/CSV.

dashboard.a: For the period you choose: policies issued and premium paid in, claims filed (by their status today), claims decided and how long that took on average, and what was paid out. Agents are ranked by premium collected on policies they sold.

staffAccounts.q: How do I add a staff member?
staffAccounts.a: In Staff, choose Add a staff member: a name, an email, a first password (same rules as registration) and a role. Give them the password privately; they can change it in their profile.

deactivate.q: What happens when I deactivate someone?
deactivate.a: They can no longer sign in, and any session they have open ends at their next click. Nothing they did is undone. Reactivating lets them sign in again with their password.

roleChange.q: What happens when I change a role?
roleChange.a: Their sessions end and they sign in again with the new role. A former agent’s customers become unassigned so you can hand them to another agent; claims a former adjuster holds stay with them, and an administrator can decide them.

lastAdmin.q: Why can’t I deactivate or demote an administrator?
lastAdmin.a: Nobody can deactivate their own account or change their own role, and at least one active administrator must always remain.

assign.q: How do customers get an agent?
assign.a: Open the customer and choose their agent under Agent. The agent then sees them and can sell to them; policies already sold stay with whoever sold them.

audit.q: What is in the audit log?
audit.a: Every claim and policy status change with who made it, and the staff actions recorded since the admin panel was added: accounts created, deactivated and reactivated, role changes and customer assignments. Earlier staff actions were not recorded, so they don’t appear.

rates.q: Can I change the base rates?
rates.a: Not here. The rates are illustrative and set with the database; the products page shows them read-only.
